record.original_question: Let f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} be computable by a DNF of size s > 1, and let epsilon in (0,1/2]. Is the Fourier spectrum of f always epsilon-concentrated on some collection F with |F| <= s^{O(log(1/epsilon))}?

evidence.quote: Statement: Let f : {-1, 1}^n -> {-1, 1} be computable by a DNF of size s > 1 and let epsilon in (0, 1/2]. Then f's Fourier spectrum is epsilon-concentrated on a collection F with |F| <= s^{O(log(1/epsilon))}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a Boolean function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, write its Fourier expansion as
$$f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]} \hat f(S)\,\chi_S(x),\qquad \chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}x_i.$$
By Parseval's identity, $\sum_{S}\hat f(S)^2=1$. For $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2]$, we say $f$ is $\varepsilon$-concentrated on a collection $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ if
$$\sum_{S\notin\mathcal F}\hat f(S)^2\le \varepsilon.$$
A DNF formula of size $s$ is a disjunction of at most $s$ terms, where each term is a conjunction of literals over $x_1,\dots,x_n$ (with $x_i\in\{-1,1\}$ interpreted as Boolean values).

Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant $C>0$ such that for every $n\ge 1$, every $s>1$, every DNF formula $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ of size at most $s$, and every $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2]$, the Fourier spectrum of $f$ is $\varepsilon$-concentrated on some collection $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ with
$$|\mathcal F|\le s^{C\log(1/\varepsilon)}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: This is Mansour's Conjecture (1994). It remains open in general. Klivans–Lee–Wan (2010) proved it for random DNFs and read-once DNFs. Lecomte–Tan (FOCS 2021) gave sharper bounds parameterized by the read number, improving Mansour's classical $s^{O(\log\log s)}$ bound for bounded-read DNFs, but the full conjecture for general DNFs remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Mansour's Conjecture is True for Random DNF Formulas
status_evidence.snippet: Klivans, Lee, and Wan: first progress on Mansour's conjecture, proving it for random and read-once DNFs.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is established only for special classes of DNFs.

status_evidence.title: Sharper bounds on the Fourier concentration of DNFs
status_evidence.snippet: Lecomte and Tan improve Mansour's bound from s^{O(log log s)} to s^{O(log log k)} for k-read DNFs.
status_evidence.claim: General Mansour conjecture still open; partial progress with improved bounds for bounded-read DNFs.
